what: If the owner stops their copy of the app and runs the checks within about half a minute, the new test for port 8765 starts a second copy of the app on 8765 over an empty temporary database and leaves it serving there for 20 seconds before it goes red. During those seconds a browser tab the owner still has open on http://127.0.0.1:8765/ talks to that empty copy: it shows no watchlists, and anything done there is lost; if the owner starts the app again in that window, it stops with the busy-port line. The spec asks that this test never fight a copy of the app on 8765. The cause is that the test treats any failure to hold 8765 itself as proof that a program is listening there, but a port the stopped app has just served pages on refuses that plain hold while nothing listens on it (the closed connections linger), and run.py, which is allowed to reuse such a port, then starts. I showed it on a free port, not 8765: after a copy serves three pages and stops, the test's hold fails with 'address in use' and the next start serves.
